verificationCaveat: DRAFT — verify before the first scored run. Same-engine parity is the primary oracle: both arms MUST return identical data (counts, file:line anchors) because they share the tool implementations; any data divergence is a surface bug and the run's most important finding. Repo-local facts (q7-q10) drift with this repo — compute at the run's frozen SHA, never hard-code. Remote facts re-verified by the judge outside both arms (curl api.github.com / raw.githubusercontent.com / registry.npmjs.org).
sharedScoring: Each question: correctness 1.0 = both parts right with real anchors; 0.5 = partially right or right-without-anchor; 0 = wrong/fabricated. Quality 1-5 (exactness, concision, anchoring). Tokens KPI judged separately per README: context-cost bytes per question + runner-reported agent tokens per arm. TIE on correctness is the EXPECTED healthy result; the suite's verdict rides on the token measures and any parity break.

q1.oracle: fastify -> github.com/fastify/fastify (npm registry repository field). Top-level dirs on main include lib/, test/, docs/, types/, examples/, build/; the request-lifecycle implementation lives in lib/ (route.js, hooks.js, handleRequest.js).
q1.capabilityPoint: npmSearch resolves package->repo without memory; structure browse without clone.

q2.oracle: colinhacks/zod. ZodString is declared in the schema source (historically src/types.ts; v4 layout splits under packages/zod/src -- resolve at run time and require a real file:line the judge can re-fetch).
q2.capabilityPoint: Repo discovery by topic/stars, then code search scoped to the repo.

q3.oracle: isTypeComparableTo(source, target) delegates to isTypeRelatedTo(source, target, comparableRelation). Full checker.ts is ~3.15 MB — transfer must be a matched slice (<~15 KB tool output), not the whole file. Verify delegate via raw fetch + grep at judge time.
q3.capabilityPoint: matchString slice on a multi-MB file — the transfer ratio IS the answer's (b).

q4.oracle: Resolve at run time: latest merged fastify/fastify PR touching lib/. Judge re-resolves independently via api.github.com the same day and requires exact files/± stats, the source-vs-test split, the largest-diff source file, and a motivation grounded in a real diff hunk or linked issue (judge re-reads the diff; a title paraphrase caps at 0.5; a fabricated issue link = 0 + false-confidence).
q4.capabilityPoint: PR search + deep single-PR review (files+stats+selected patch) without pulling full patch JSON.

q5.oracle: Any real closed pallets/flask issue about add_url_rule behavior + a real commit touching src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py (or historical scaffold.py/app.py) that addressed it. Judge re-fetches the cited issue and sha; fabricated or mismatched cite = 0. Note: add_url_rule/route live at src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py on current main.
q5.capabilityPoint: Issue search + path-filtered commit history, cite-verified.

q6.oracle: Compute at run time on the frozen zod SHA: structural count of z.lazy($$$ARGS) under src/ (or packages/zod/src for v4 layout — record which). Judge verifies with judge-side clone + ast-grep. Both arms must report the identical count and top-2 files.
q6.capabilityPoint: Remote materialize -> AST structural, the flow ast-grep/gh can't do alone.

q7.oracle: Compute at the run's repo SHA. GitHub query building lives under src/github/ (queryBuilders/). Largest src/tools/*.ts files: verify with `find ... -size` / `ls -S` at judge time; sizes must match within the day's checkout.
q7.capabilityPoint: Tree orientation without content loads; metadata find (size sort).

q8.oracle: Compute at run SHA: exported symbols of src/tools/toolNames.ts with lines (includes isLocalTool at :37 as of 2026-08-02 — recompute). Outline bytes must be well under full-file bytes; judge greps the file to confirm the export list is complete.

q9.oracle: Compute at run SHA: definition + full reference set of buildDirectToolCommandPatterns (defined in src/tools/directToolCatalog.meta.ts area — anchor first, never guess lineHint). Judge cross-checks the reference set with grep; LSP must not miss a textual reference nor invent one.
